title: Doing more with fewer people: How AI is changing Chinese companies
key_facts: CNA reports there were reportedly more than 16 million one-person companies in China as of June 2025.
Zhang Pengtao, 37, runs ACE Studio alone using OpenAI's coding agent Codex; he says work that took three days now takes about three hours.
By his own estimate his income is 60 to 80 per cent higher than when he ran a seven-person studio, after about US$3,000 a month on AI tools.
A Beijing community, WaytoAGI Moshu, with government support, offers space for one-person and small AI-run businesses and selected 56 of 600+ applicants.
Ant Digital Technologies says its AI assistant DT Claw can produce an investment research report in minutes against three to four hours for a senior analyst (company claim).
An Ant executive says staff resistance is the biggest obstacle and that some jobs will be affected in the short term but more people will be needed in the long term.
quote_evidence: There were reportedly more than 16 million such businesses nationwide as of June 2025.
“What used to take three days can now be done in about three hours.”
“During this period of AI transformation, some jobs will definitely be affected in the short term. But in the long term, more and more people will be needed,” he said.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows AI letting very small teams do work that needed staff, with limits and company claims.
notes: Income and time savings are the interviewee's own estimates; Ant's report-speed claim is company-stated.
